title: Redwood private VPC security architecture deep dive with Aurora Capital
next_steps: Share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 reports (Redwood)
Send detailed network diagram and VPC peering options (Redwood SE)
Customer to provide list of required egress IPs and data residency constraints
Schedule on-prem POC kickoff for week of 2025-04-21
action_items: Maya Patel: Share SOC 2 & ISO reports (due 2025-04-04)
Ethan Cho: Produce VPC/network diagram and proposed security controls (due 2025-04-07)
Raj Singh: Provide egress IP whitelist and compliance checklist (due 2025-04-10)
transcript: Meeting header: 2025-04-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~75 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Aurora Head of Security), Raj (Aurora Cloud Architect), Oliver (CTO)

Summary: Private/VPC security deep dive focusing on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, audit logs, and key management. Customer wants air-gapped/on-prem options and strong RBAC/SSO assurances. Redwood to share compliance pack and network diagrams.

Topics: SOC 2/ISO evidence; RBAC & SSO (SAML); audit log delivery & retention; encryption/BYOK (KMS/HSM); network isolation patterns (VPC endpoints, PrivateLink, peering); ingress/egress controls, firewalling and egress proxies; on-prem / air-gapped constraints.

[00:00] Maya: Hey thanks everyone for taking the time, quick intros then we'll dive into the network diagram. Ethan is our solutions engineer, he'll walk the architecture. Lena, Raj, want to kick off intros?,

[00:22] Lena: Yep. Lena Torres, Head of Security at Aurora. We're responsible for compliance and secure deployment. Main concerns: data residency, auditability, and controlling egress. We also need SOC 2 and ISO artifacts.
[00:38] Raj: Raj Singh, Cloud Architect. We're on AWS primarily, some Azure for DR. Want to understand VPC options and how Redwood handles private traffic and ingress/egress firewalling.

[01:05] Ethan: Cool, thanks. Quick agenda: compliance evidence, auth (SSO/SAML, RBAC), KMS/BYOK, then detailed networking: private endpoints, peering, ingress controllers, NAT/egress, firewall rules, and monitoring (flow logs, audit logs).
[02:00] Maya: One note, we'll also cover the on-prem package and air-gapped options briefly — what that looks like operationally and for updates.

[03:15] Ethan: Ok jumping into compliance. Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001. We can share the reports under NDA — they include control mappings for access control, change management, and logging. (slight pause) I'll drop the report link after the call.

[03:47] Lena: Great, we usually validate controls against our rubric. We'll need the scope (production infra vs control plane). Also, retention for audit logs — do you retain customer-facing logs or do you push logs to customer SIEM?

[04:10] Ethan: Good question. For Private deployments we support forwarding audit logs to customer endpoints — e.g., CloudWatch/Kinesis, Event Hubs, or syslog into a SIEM. We can also mirror logs to a customer S3 bucket in the region for retention. For Hosted there's a different model. We'll share the exact log schema.
[05:00] Raj: For network, we need specifics: does Redwood require any inbound open internet IPs? How is ingress handled for private VPC?

[05:22] Ethan: With private VPC we offer three patterns: 1) VPC peering to a Redwood VPC (managed private cross-account) 2) AWS PrivateLink/Interface Endpoints 3) Fully customer-hosted on-prem deployment. For peering and PrivateLink, you keep all traffic within AWS backbone. Ingress is via interface endpoints — no public load balancer exposed to the internet unless you opt in.
[06:10] Raj: Ok and egress? We need to enforce strict egress via our NAT + customer-managed proxy and block direct internet egress except for specific services.

[06:30] Ethan: We support that. You can configure no direct internet egress — Redwood nodes will route outbound to your NAT gateway. For hosted control plane calls, there's an option to route control plane through a customer-managed egress. For entirely air-gapped on-prem, there is zero outbound by default unless you provide an update pipeline.
[07:05] Lena: How about firewalling — security groups vs NACLs vs host-based? We have a strict baseline (deny-all ingress, allow-list egress where possible).

[07:22] Ethan: Best practice is layered controls: security groups for instance-level allow lists (port-level), NACLs for subnet-level rules, and optionally host-based firewalls inside the instance. For Redwood Dedicated nodes we allow you to push a config that locks down management ports and only allows internal control plane traffic from customer subnets.
[08:00] Oliver: Do you terminate TLS at your LB or inside our VPC? We require mutual TLS for service-to-service in some workloads.

[08:20] Ethan: We offer two modes: TLS termination at your ALB (you manage certs) or mTLS end-to-end with Redwood mutual auth. For PrivateLink, you can terminate on your side and enforce mTLS between your services and Redwood endpoints. We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and FIPS-compliant ciphers on request.
[09:10] Raj: KMS and BYOK is a big one. We need to control keys for data at rest, model caches, and any stored artifacts. What integrations exist with AWS KMS or HSMs?

[09:34] Ethan: We support BYOK: you can provide keys in your KMS, and Redwood uses a customer-managed key for encrypting the volumes and object storage. For HSMs we integrate via CloudHSM and can support HSM-backed keys for the private deployment. There's a small ops integration to rotate keys and to handle rewrapping during upgrades.
[10:05] Lena: And what about K/V cache and in-memory tokens — are they encrypted?

[10:18] Ethan: KV cache is encrypted at rest and in transit. In-memory is protected by process isolation and we minimize persisted sensitive tokens. If you require, we can place sensitive caches on ephemeral disks that are encrypted with your KMS keys.

[11:00] Maya: quick note — you asked about audit logs earlier: we also emit comprehensive audit trails for admin actions, model rollouts, and route changes. These can be forwarded with immutable retention policies if required.
[11:45] Raj: Flow logs and VPC reachability — we want to run network-level audits and detect any unexpected egress. Can we get flow logs for the subnets and integrate with our SIEM?

[12:05] Ethan: Yes, flow logs can be exported to your account's CloudWatch or S3. We can also enable enhanced networking telemetry and forward to a Kinesis stream for real-time detection. Customers often pipe to Splunk/QRadar via Kinesis or syslog collectors.
[13:10] Lena: For SSO and RBAC — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Can Redwood map roles to our groups and enforce least privilege?

[13:32] Ethan: We support SAML SSO with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based and you can map your groups to roles (admin, ops, read-only). We also support session durations and MFA enforcement via the IdP.

[14:20] Maya: A small caveat — some of the terming in our docs is Redwood Private vs Redwood Dedicated, so apologies if the transcript mis-mentions product names. We'll include an architecture doc that calls out the exact config options.
[14:45] Raj: Do you provide ingress IP ranges for firewall whitelisting? We need a stable list of egress/ingress IPs for our perimeter firewall.

[15:00] Ethan: For PrivateLink and peering, ingress is within the VPC, so no public IPs necessary. For situations where we do have to cross accounts, we can provide a set of NAT egress IPs or allow you to set up a static NAT. We'll provide the list of IP ranges and also support a Lambda to rotate them if needed.
[16:12] Lena: Regulatory: data residency. We need guarantees that data doesn't leave EU region for EU customers. How do you enforce this?

[16:30] Ethan: We allow you to pin regions and we provide region-specific deployments. For Private we deploy into your region and can configure storage to remain in-region. We'll document where logs and backups live; we also support contractual commitments around data residency in the enterprise agreement.
[17:05] Oliver: On-prem option — what does lifecycle/updates look like? We have air-gapped racks and can't allow outbound updates except via signed packages.

[17:28] Ethan: For on-prem, we provide an air-gap installer and signed artifacts. Patches are applied via an update bundle you pull from a secure staging bucket. We support signing and verification; there's a documented process for patch delivery and rollbacks.
[18:00] Raj: Any dependencies on external SaaS? For example telemetry or usage collection?

[18:15] Ethan: For private/on-prem we minimize external telemetry. Optional telemetry can be configured to send anonymized usage metrics back to Redwood; it's off by default in air-gapped installs. Control plane integration can be run via a private peered control plane or a customer-managed control plane.
[19:10] Lena: How do you handle incidents — access to logs during an incident and auditability?

[19:28] Ethan: We provide a runbook and support for incident response. For Private we can grant time-limited access to our SREs via bastion or via delegated roles you provision. All access is logged and included in the audit trail. We can also stream those logs to your SIEM.
[20:00] (interruption) Speaker 1: uh can I just clarify — what's the overhead for encryption performance?

[20:10] Ethan: There's a small CPU overhead for envelope encryption using your KMS; in practice it's <5% for IO-heavy workloads. For model inference we rely on GPU memory and ephemeral caches; disk encryption is mostly transparent.
[21:00] Maya: We're approaching the middle — quick poll: is the customer's primary blocker anything we haven't covered?
[21:12] Raj: Main blockers: precise egress IPs, BYOK confirmations, and the air-gap upgrade process. If those are satisfied we can proceed to POC.

[22:00] Ethan: On the POC — we propose a small Dedicated deployment in your AWS account with VPC peering and audit log forwarding. We'll run a set of latency/cost benchmarks and a security checklist. That should surface any remaining concerns.
[23:30] Lena: For the security checklist we'll need a mapping to our internal controls (we'll send the checklist).
[24:00] Ethan: Perfect. We'll map Redwood controls to your rubric and provide an evidence pack. We'll also include the network diagram and example security group/NACL configs.

[25:20] Maya: Quick notes on artifacts we'll share: SOC 2 & ISO reports (NDA), network diagram, sample terraform for peering/endpoints, audit log schema, BYOK integration doc, on-prem installer overview. Links will be pushed to the thread.
[26:45] Raj: What about pen testing and vulnerability scans? We have a policy requiring annual pen tests for any third-party infra.

[27:10] Ethan: We do regular internal and third-party pen tests. For Private deployments we can share summary reports and coordinate scoping if Aurora wants to do a managed pentest against the deployed environment — we usually require a test plan and a window.
[28:05] Lena: Regarding retention — our rule is 7 years for some logs. Can Redwood support long-term archival?

[28:25] Ethan: Yes, logs can be forwarded to your S3 with lifecycle policies for long-term retention. For very long retention we recommend immutable storage with object lock if you need WORM semantics.
[29:10] Oliver: A couple quick nit picks: do you have FIPS modes, and can you meet our crypto certs?
[29:30] Ethan: FIPS and HSM-backed KMS are supported in the Private/on-prem variant. We'll clarify which kernels/ciphers are enabled and produce a cryptographic profile for your security team.
[30:00] (crosstalk) Lena: ok cool, thanks.

[31:15] Maya: Recap before we wrap: Redwood to share compliance pack and architecture docs; Ethan to provide network diagram and sample firewall rules; Aurora provides egress IP list and internal control checklist. We'll schedule POC kickoff week of 4/21. Any other asks?
[31:50] Raj: Please include sample terraform and IAM policies for the peered setup — we prefer IaC for audits.
[32:05] Ethan: Will do. We'll include terraform snippets and sample IAM role defs.
[33:00] Lena: One last ask — can we get a short threat model for the private deployment? We want a 1-2 page doc mapping possible threats and mitigations.
[33:20] Ethan: Yep we have a template; will adapt it for the Aurora POC.
[34:00] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send the thread with the attachments and proposed dates. Meeting adjourned.

- Redwood: Share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 under NDA
- Redwood SE: Network diagram, terraform snippets, sample SG/NACL rules, BYOK doc, audit log schema

- All: Schedule POC kickoff week of 2025-04-21
